newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Suharto urges business to narrow gap.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Suharto urges business to narrow gap.

text.p: Indonesian President Suharto on Saturday urged local corporate leaders to bridge the growing gap between large, medium and small business.

"We can all witness the growth, but the problem now is that our economy's growth is dominated by a certain group," Suharto told businessmen during a meeting in the Bogor palace, some 60 km (37 miles) south of Jakarta.
"We must overcome this... because our development aims to give prosperity to as many people as possible, not only for a certain group," Suharto said.

Suharto did not name the group in his speech to the meeting of venture capitalists, but the Indonesian economy is dominated by corporations controlled by ethnic Chinese businessmen, a number of whom were present at the meeting.
He said economic growth in the nation of more than 200 million people was essential.
"But the domination by a certain group now becomes a political issue," he said.
Analysts have blamed the gap between rich and poor for a number of riots in Indonesia in the past year.
While many businesses have expanded as the Indonesian economy grew at more than seven percent a year, the average annual incomes remains only about $1,000.
Suharto admitted that the growth of small- and medium-size businesses was slow and this widened the gap between them and the large conglomerates.
"We must help the small and medium businesses with capital through venture capital so they can speed up," Suharto said.
He said the government had issued a number of programmes to help small and medium business.
Suharto in December issued a decree to order wealthy Indonesian individuals and companies to donate two percent of their income to poor through a government-run charitable foundation.
